title: Nearest Price Match Across Two Catalogs
description:
Two product catalogs (`catalog_a` and `catalog_b`) each list products with prices. For each product in `catalog_a`, **find the closest price match** from `catalog_b` (minimum absolute price difference). If there is a tie, return the catalog_b product with the lower `product_id`.

**Tables: catalog_a, catalog_b**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| product_id | INT |
| product_name | VARCHAR |
| price | NUMERIC(10,2) |

Output columns: `a_id`, `a_name`, `a_price`, `b_id`, `b_name`, `b_price`, `price_diff`. Order by `a_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE catalog_a (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, price NUMERIC(10,2)); INSERT INTO catalog_a VALUES (1,'Widget Pro',29.99),(2,'Gadget X',149.99),(3,'Doohickey',9.99),(4,'Thingamajig',299.99),(5,'Gizmo Elite',79.99),(6,'Device Plus',199.99); CREATE TABLE catalog_b (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, price NUMERIC(10,2)); INSERT INTO catalog_b VALUES (101,'Widget Premium',32.50),(102,'Gadget Y',145.00),(103,'Doohickey Lite',8.99),(104,'Thingamajig Pro',310.00),(105,'Gizmo Basic',74.99),(106,'Device Standard',185.00),(107,'Widget Basic',24.99),(108,'Mega Gadget',499.99);
solution_sql: WITH price_matches AS (SELECT a.product_id AS a_id, a.product_name AS a_name, a.price AS a_price, b.product_id AS b_id, b.product_name AS b_name, b.price AS b_price, ABS(a.price - b.price) AS price_diff, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.product_id ORDER BY ABS(a.price - b.price), b.product_id) AS rn FROM catalog_a a CROSS JOIN catalog_b b) SELECT a_id, a_name, a_price, b_id, b_name, b_price, price_diff FROM price_matches WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY a_id

test_cases.description: Closest catalog_b match for each catalog_a product

hints: CROSS JOIN catalog_a with catalog_b to generate all (a, b) product pairs, then compute ABS(a.price - b.price) as the price difference. This is O(n×m) but straightforward for catalog-sized datasets.

Apply ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.product_id ORDER BY ABS(a.price - b.price), b.product_id) to rank catalog_b matches for each catalog_a product. Filter WHERE rn = 1 to keep only the best match, with b.product_id as a tiebreaker.
explanation: A CROSS JOIN generates every possible pairing between the two catalogs. For each catalog_a product, ROW_NUMBER() ranks all catalog_b matches in ascending order of price difference, using b.product_id as a secondary sort for tie-breaking. Filtering to rn = 1 retains only the closest match. Notable results: Widget Pro (29.99) matches Widget Premium (32.50) with a diff of just 2.51 — closer than Widget Basic (24.99, diff=5.00); Gadget X (149.99) matches Gadget Y (145.00) with a 4.99 difference; Doohickey (9.99) matches Doohickey Lite (8.99) at only 1.00 difference. The CROSS JOIN approach is O(n×m) so it works well for small-to-medium catalog sizes; for large catalogs, approximate matching with bucketing or similarity search is preferred.
